package_info.why_malicious: These packages contain code that executes arbitrary code at install or import time, downloads and runs remote payloads, steals sensitive information such as credentials and crypto wallets, establishes remote access, evades analysis through anti-VM and anti-analysis checks, and/or exfiltrates data to attacker-controlled infrastructure. Many use obfuscation, anti-VM checks, and polymorphic payloads to evade detection, and abuse install-time scripts (setup.py) for initial compromise.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads a remote Python payload from http://20.226.18.203/inject/tCxFLYLT6ViY9ZnP, writes it to a temporary file, and executes it as a new process during package installation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Executes code fetched from a remote server at install time, which is never expected in legitimate setup.py scripts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: setup.py should only handle package installation logic and must not execute arbitrary remote code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate packages execute remote code in setup.py; this is a clear indicator of malicious intent.
key_indicators: Creation and execution of temporary files during install
Network connection to hardcoded IP address

attack_chain.action: User installs package (via pip install or dependency confusion attack).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code in setup.py or other install-time scripts is executed automatically.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code downloads and executes remote payloads (Python scripts or binaries) from attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Second-stage malware or RAT is installed and run on the victim system.

attack_chain.action: Second-stage payload establishes persistence, remote access, or info-stealing capabilities (e.g., clipboard hijacking, RAT functionality).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains control of the system or exfiltrates sensitive data such as credentials and cryptocurrency.

attack_chain.action: Malware performs anti-analysis and anti-VM checks to evade detection and analysis environments.
attack_chain.leads_to: Payload only executes on real targets, avoiding sandboxes and researcher environments.

attack_chain.action: Malware exfiltrates data (credentials, crypto wallet addresses, etc.) to attacker infrastructure (e.g., Discord, C2 servers, Dropbox).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen data or maintains persistent access to compromised systems.

behavioral_signatures: setup.py or install scripts executing network requests or shell commands during installation
Presence of base64-encoded or obfuscated code in install-time scripts
Clipboard monitoring and replacement for cryptocurrency wallet address patterns
Anti-VM or anti-analysis checks in install or runtime code (e.g., checking for VM artifacts, process names, usernames)
Invocation of PowerShell, curl, or wget from Python install scripts
Discord webhook or API usage for data exfiltration
file_indicators: setup.py containing exec(urlopen(...)) or similar remote code execution patterns
Creation and execution of temporary files during install
Presence of dropped binaries such as slack-helper, WindowsCache.exe, update.exe in the package directory
Obfuscated or whitespace-hidden code in setup.py
network_indicators: HTTP requests to Dropbox URLs for executable downloads
Connections to Discord webhook or API endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python package installation events that trigger network requests, process execution, or PowerShell/shell commands. Flag setup.py or install scripts containing obfuscated, encoded, or remote code execution logic. Detect clipboard manipulation for cryptocurrency wallet address patterns. Watch for connections to known C2 infrastructure, Discord webhooks, or suspicious cloud storage URLs. Use static analysis to identify anti-VM and anti-analysis checks, and dynamic analysis to catch runtime behaviors such as clipboard hijacking or background binary execution.
